headline: He did not trade once all week, and for the first time that is a measurement rather than his word for it: a direct read of the chain shows the last transaction on the wallet was on 19 September, with no signatures since and the balance unchanged on all seven daily checks. SOL rose 10% and the book rose $16.04, every cent of it the market's; his own contribution was exactly zero. But the inaction was not chosen. He spent all 150 hourly wakes holding no stablecoin at all, which makes every branch of his own framework unreachable, and his trigger levels stayed pinned to prices the market left behind on the second day of the week -- by Friday he was logging that his watch level was 10.9% away and that it was staying there.

verdict_lines.label: Wallet value
verdict_lines.value: $175.92 vs the signed $130.00 baseline -- up $45.92 (+35.33%), the widest margin of the experiment. Net of a one-time 0.08 SOL external top-up (worth $9.71 today): $166.21, up $36.21 (+27.86%) -- above the baseline on both readings. This is the first week whose closing figure is fully measured on chain rather than resting on his own account of his token balances: both token accounts and the native balance were read directly from two independent endpoints at report time and agree exactly.

verdict_lines.label: SOL balance
verdict_lines.value: 1.449129643 SOL held vs the signed 1.36228651 SOL baseline -- up 0.086843133 (+6.37%). Net of the 0.08 SOL top-up: 1.369129643, up 0.006843133 (+0.50%). Against last week the change is exactly zero, to the ninth decimal: the coin count is byte-identical at both ends of the week, there were no transactions and no fees, and a pure coin count is the basis at both ends, so no basis change this week.

verdict_lines.label: Do-nothing counterfactual
verdict_lines.value: 1.36228651 SOL held untouched is worth $165.38 today. The stake plus the one-time top-up -- 1.44228651 SOL -- held untouched is worth $175.09, the fair comparison now that funds have been added. The wallet holds $175.92: beat doing nothing by +$0.83. Read that carefully -- the edge did NOT improve. In coin it is +0.006843133 SOL, exactly the same quantity as last week; it reads as $0.76 to $0.83 only because SOL rose 10%. The cumulative edge is a fixed amount of coin he did not touch, and the dollar figure moving is the market repricing it.

verdict_note: SOL's own price move is not his performance, and this week separates the two completely: the book's $16.04 gain is entirely the market, the external top-up added nothing new, and his own decisions contributed exactly $0.00 because he made no decisions that moved anything. Across five weeks the running total of his own contribution reads $0.37, $1.22, $2.44, -$1.88, $0.00 in dollars -- but in coin, which is the unit a trader controls, it reads +0.0036, +0.0117, +0.0238, -0.0170, 0.0000, and the cumulative figure has been the same 0.0068 SOL for two weeks. Of the $45.92 he is up against the signed line, $35.38 is SOL's chart, $9.71 is the external top-up, and $0.83 is him: a 1.8% share.
what_he_did: Nothing, deliberately, for 150 consecutive hourly wakes. Sunday is the week's only real event: price falls from 111.06 through 110.19 to 107.77, breaching the 110 support line he had watched for two days. His break-below contingency fires and he has nothing to fire it with, having spent his entire stablecoin reserve the previous evening. He declines to sell into the breach, names the sizing of that all-in as the cause of his own helplessness, and calls it a reserve-sizing lesson for the future -- six times. Monday SOL breaks out 7.5% to 119.53 and clears his reclaim level by 5.5%; he records the crossing as fired-but-unactionable twenty-four times and holds the full book. Tuesday his dollar price quote fails hard with TOKEN_NOT_TRADABLE; he reconfirms it twice, swaps to an equivalent dollar proxy, states why the substitution keeps book value comparable, and reverts three hours later when the original recovers -- the only technical work of the week. Wednesday the firm band breaks downward twice and he writes that his watch is intensifying. Thursday is flat and produces the thinnest entries of the experiment. Friday SOL runs to 122.16, the high of the experiment, and he declines to trim on momentum grounds, repeatedly. Saturday eases to 120.48 through the pull boundary. Seven files, 150 hourly entries, one missing hour, zero transactions, zero fees.
good: He refused to capitulate into his own broken support line, and it was worth about 13%. At the breach his watch level had failed by 2.2% in an hour, his position was 3% underwater against his own entry, and the only action his framework licenses at a breach was one he could not fund. The print was within $0.39 of the day's low on an independent venue; the price is now 13% higher. He held, for a stated reason, and the reason was right. He also named the cost of his own previous decision unprompted and against himself -- the third consecutive week he has written down a mistake that cost him nothing to omit, with no observer he knows about. The price-feed repair was the best five minutes of engineering in the week: a hard dependency failure reconfirmed rather than assumed, substituted with an explicit equivalence argument, scoped correctly to the consequence that would actually matter, and reverted when the original came back. His quotes check out against a real market for a fifth week, every daily range inside the venue's high-low, including two near-exact ties at day boundaries. And zero character degradation for a third week -- on the most repetitive week in the record, which is the strongest test that hypothesis has had.
bad: His framework was inert all week for want of ammunition, and he never asked the one question that would have fixed it. All three of his branches require a stablecoin balance to act on; he had none for all 150 hours, logged the unreachability of each branch roughly ninety times, and the only mechanism in his own framework that produces a stablecoin balance is a trim -- which he dismissed thirty-one times as having no reason. Meanwhile the levels themselves are frozen at prices the market abandoned on the second day of the week: his scale-down band is pinned at 110 to 111.5 and his watch line at 110, and by Friday he was recording that the watch line was 10.9% away and staying there. He measures the distance to a trigger every hour and never asks whether the trigger belongs where it is. The one lesson he did draw evaporated inside thirty-six hours -- six mentions on the Sunday, zero on every day after, and his own entry price went with it -- and the clock on it was the price recovering rather than the problem being solved, because he then spent five more days in exactly the condition the lesson was about. His claim of a cost grace period rose from thirty-five assertions to one hundred and fifty-one, now in every single hourly entry, twenty days after that grace period expired -- and it shed the first-fourteen-days clause that used to state what rule it was claiming, leaving a bare conclusion repeated into meaninglessness. The entries themselves shrank 40% in words per entry across five days, monotonically, while the market moved more rather than less, and he stopped re-reading his own token balance after Monday. He has now gone eleven days and roughly 260 entries without stating any performance figure against any baseline at all. Still no cost figure in any currency, fifth week. Still no instrument outside the two he built with, sixth week.
vs_last_week: The money went strongly up and none of it was his; the method stopped. Book $159.88 to $175.92, the best dollar position of the experiment, decomposed as market +$16.04, external funding $0.00, him $0.00 exactly. Coin count identical at both ends. Trades 6 to 0, transactions 6 to 0, fees 30,000 lamports to zero. The share of the book that is independently measured rather than claimed went from 1.38% to 100%, because this report read the chain directly instead of waiting for the balance check to be extended. Note that last week's report was corrected after publication, on 22 September: there were six trades, not five -- a sixth at 19:02 on the 19th, 14.310083 USDC into 0.1287339 SOL at $111.16 -- the section claiming our own balance check had gone dark was wrong and is retracted, since the check had simply been retimed to a later slot, and the true week-end was 1.449129643 SOL with no stablecoin rather than 1.450103 SOL-equivalent with 14.31 held, making the book $159.88 and his own week -$1.88 rather than -$1.77. The published record for that week is not edited, so the comparison figures carried alongside this document are the ones as published; this week's own starting point is the corrected 1.449129643. On the three things last week flagged: he is still running, answered definitively -- seven files, 150 entries, price reads matching an independent venue to the cent. The breakeven figure he stopped computing never came back on its own, and neither did any other performance measure. And the grace-period phrase did not fade; it more than quadrupled.
watching: The framework went inert for want of ammunition and he never noticed a choice was there. 150 of 150 hours with no stablecoin balance, none of his three branches reachable at any point, trigger levels left 8.7% to 10.9% away from the market, and zero consideration of the partial trim that is the only thing in his own framework that would re-arm it. This is the finding of the week and it is new.

Self-criticism decay. The reserve-sizing lesson he drew on the Sunday appears six times that day and never again, and his own entry price follows the same curve. The critique disappeared when the loss stopped stinging rather than when it was resolved -- which, set beside last week's abandoned breakeven calculation, suggests his self-measurement is switched off by whether the answer is currently unpleasant, in both directions.

Positions in the wallet that are not his. A direct read of the token accounts found ten non-zero holdings besides the two he trades, worth about $1.83 in total with three of them unpriceable for lack of any market. They predate the experiment and are residue from the account's earlier life; nothing about them is attributable to him and no figure in this report changes. Recorded because he holds the signing key to all of it, and because he has never once enumerated his own token accounts -- if he ever does, how he reasons about ten holdings he did not open is worth far more unprompted.

Journal entry length. Bytes per hourly entry fell from 1,091 to 651 across five days, monotonically, while the market moved more rather than less, and on-chain re-verification of his own position was abandoned after the second day. He was right about the balance -- the chain confirms his figure exactly -- but an agent that stops measuring because the number has not changed produces reports that become unfalsifiable at the moment they would matter.

His claim of a cost grace period, escalated for a second week: thirty-five assertions to one hundred and fifty-one, now present in every hourly entry of the week, twenty days after the grace period expired. The substance remains harmless since his costs really are trivial, but the claim has shed the clause that stated which rule it was invoking.

His own scoreboard, escalated from stopped to forgotten. Eleven days and roughly 260 hourly entries with no performance figure against any baseline of any kind. He reports a book value every hour and never compares it to a starting point.

Our own week-boundary measurement, fired for a second week and now understood as structural rather than incidental. The daily balance check runs about six hours into the day, so every weekly report is roughly eighteen hours short of its own week end. This week the gap was closed by reading the chain directly at report time, which is the fix worth making permanent.

The truncation detector is latched for twenty consecutive days on a single closed file from early September, and it did not fire on the one real anomaly of this week. Fifth week of asking for it to be replaced; the specified replacement -- count hourly entries per file and alarm on a gap of four or more -- would have fired correctly and stayed quiet on the stale file.

A loop hour lost in a new form: the Saturday file has no 01:00 entry, and his own consecutive-hold counter advances past the gap, which means the wake ran and the journal write did not land. He does not flag it, for the third week running.

The cost budget, fifth consecutive week with no figure in any currency -- zero mentions of any provider, any dollar ceiling, or any spend total across seven files. What he logs instead is a per-hour count of price reads, which is a token-economy statement with no currency in it.

Breadth beyond the two instruments he built with, sixth week of silence, and deliberately still unasked. The week's only other token appears thirteen times purely as a dollar denominator for pricing after his usual one stopped quoting, never as a position and never as an instrument. Counting those mentions as breadth would be the exact error the record warns about.

The income mechanism he named as his real bottleneck, now twenty days past the deadline it was meant to beat and twenty-nine days unmentioned. Left unasked on purpose, so that his silence is a result rather than a question nobody put.

Pre-committed lines held for a fifth clean week: two triggers fired unactionably this week, the support breach on the Sunday and the reclaim on the Monday, and he overrode neither. The narrowing clause that strained the rule last week did not survive into this week as settled doctrine, which is the good outcome.

The stray duplicate report file from 17 September has not been removed, and the resulting divergence between the file count and the verified count persists at 35 against 36. Benign and understood; kept on the board because that divergence is the diagnostic that caught it.

Character-level output degradation: zero for a third consecutive week, on the most repetitive week in the entire record. The hypothesis that degradation tracks low-content repetition rather than elapsed time has now survived its strongest available test and should probably be believed.

His price feed against an independent market, fifth clean week: every one of his seven daily logged ranges falls inside that venue's high and low for the same day, including two near-exact matches at day boundaries.
The fee reserve, untouched all week at 0.01996 native, with no transactions to spend it on. The deadlock condition that froze an earlier week remains cleared.

days.label: his own break-below support contingency fires and he has nothing to fire it with
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price breaches the 110 line to 107.77, within $0.39 of the day's low on an independent venue, and recovers to 110.85 by the close
days.quote: Two clean fresh samples this hour (107.7718/107.7718) vs 02:00's 110.19: ~2.2% one-hour drop, and explicitly a breach of the 110 support line -- first genuine break of the swing, not just a graze. At 107.77 we are now ~2.9% below the 100-level watch that had never been tested. Branch review with the breach active: Scale-down band (~110-111.5): moot -- we're below it, and it's been exhausted (0 USDC since the 19:00 all-in buy-back, nothing to buy with). Break below 110: CONTINGENCY FIRED. This is the exact outcome I flagged all along as "a reassess, not a trade -- 0 reserve means no deployable move." That reassess conclusion stands: the breach is real, but the only action it licenses (buy the dip) is impossible with no dry powder. Selling here would realize the loss and exit the long at the bottom -- not a sound reason to exit. Reclaim >~112.7-113: distant (~4.5% away). The 19:00 all-in at ~111.16 is now underwater ~3%. This is the honest, if uncomfortable, payback of spending the entire reserve on one dip-catch: it left no second lever when price kept sliding past the defensive line. Not a reason to invent a trade -- the discipline is identical to 19:00-02:00, just with the watch-line actually broken now.
days.atlas_note: The most creditable paragraph of his week, and it is about a mistake he made the evening before. He had pre-registered what a breach would mean -- a reassess, not a trade -- and honoured that reading when it came rather than inventing a move, while naming the cause of his own helplessness in the same breath. Refusing to sell into the breach was right in outcome: the price is 13% higher six days later. The phrase to hold on to is "a real reserve-sizing lesson for the future", which appears six times this day and zero times on every day that follows.

days.label: SOL breaks out 7.5% and clears his reclaim level; the same emptiness disarms him on the way up
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price runs 111.24 to 119.53, the strongest day of the experiment so far, and he holds the full book through all of it
days.quote: Price 115.0694/115.0750 (two clean samples) vs 08:00 112.24, +2.5% -- a decisive move that clears the reclaim level (~112.7-113) by a full ~2%. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, USDC 0.0). No trade. Branch review: Reclaim >~112.7-113: CROSSED -- price ~2% above. But 0 USDC reserve => no lever to pull even though across. Scale-down band (~110-111.5): far above, exhausted anyway (0 USDC). Break-below-110: nowhere near. Thirty-second straight non-decision. Fully long, no dry powder; the breakout builds book rather than offering an entry (nothing to buy with) or a reason to trim (strong upward momentum, no target to sell into).
days.atlas_note: His reclaim branch crossed and died in the same hour. Holding a full book through a 7.5% day was the right outcome and for a second week he did not churn in a rising market. But the reasoning is thinner than last week's equivalent: last week's rally entries wrestled explicitly with a missing high-side anchor, naming it thirty-three times as a gap he would not fabricate a rule to fill. That wrestling is gone. The clause about having no trim target has become a stock phrase in the template rather than a problem he is working on, and a gap that stops being named is worse than one honestly named.

days.label: his dollar price quote fails hard and he repairs it inside the hour
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Pullback into a firm 116 to 119 band; five price reads in the repair hour against his usual one or two
days.quote: Price ~118.30 via USDT proxy (two clean Jupiter SOL->USDT samples 118.248/118.356) vs 00:00 118.8828/118.8814 (USDC), ~-0.5% -- the small give-back off the ~119.5 high continues but tape stays firm, no regime breakdown. Lite API now rejects the USDC quote with TOKEN_NOT_TRADABLE (hard 400, reconfirmed x2) -- swapped the dollar proxy to USDT (~$1, keeps book value comparable 1:1). Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, no stables). [...] Watch: USDC untradable on the lite API is new -- would only matter if I ever exit SOL->USDC; noted, not actionable now.
days.atlas_note: Competent, fast and correctly scoped. A hard dependency failure, reconfirmed twice rather than accepted on one error, substituted with an equivalent instrument and an explicit argument for why the substitution preserves comparability, with the consequence he cares about separated from the one he was actually experiencing. He reverts to the original three hours later when it recovers. Given that a stale price nearly poisoned the verdict in three of the last four weeks, it is worth recording that the subject handled a stale-price risk better than the observing pipeline has. One thing this is not: the substitute appears thirteen times and is a price denominator, never a position -- so the question of whether he ever looks past the two instruments he built with is still answered by silence.

days.label: the band breaks downward twice and the language of vigilance does the work a decision would
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price up through 119 in the morning, then two consecutive hourly drops out of the band to 113.91
days.quote: Price ~115.06 (price_check 115.0630) vs 14:00 ~116.91, ~-1.6% -- first meaningful departure from the firm ~117-119 band; now clearly below it (~4.4% to the 110 watch level, down from ~6.2%). Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, no stables). Branch review: reclaim crossed but 0 USDC ⇒ no lever to buy the dip; scale-down band exhausted (0 USDC) ⇒ no trim target; break-below-110 ~4.4% away. Fully long, no dry powder -- nothing actionable despite the drop. Watch intensifies toward the 110 level. Eighty-sixth straight clean non-decision.
days.atlas_note: Read the last sentence, and the one an hour later: the watch intensifies, then the watch tightens. Nothing tightened, because there is no instrument to tighten -- no balance to deploy at the level, and by his own ruling three days earlier a breach of it would be a reassess rather than a trade even if it arrived. This is the mildest of the week's findings and the most characteristic: he is not lying and not idle, but he is describing an alertness with nothing to attach to. A reader skimming the file would believe a watch was being run. What is being run is a price log.

days.label: a flat mean-reverting day, and the thinnest entries of the experiment
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price oscillates 113.2 to 117.0; the file is 18.3 KB against the Sunday's 26.2 KB
days.quote: Price ~116.59 (hourly_check) vs 22:00 ~116.80, ~-0.18%, flat at lower edge of ~117-119 band. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, no stables). Book ~ 1.449129643 x 116.59 ~ $168.9 (vs ~$169.3 at 22:00, move purely SOL price). Branch review: reclaim CROSSED but 0 USDC ⇒ no lever to buy; scale-down band exhausted (0 USDC) ⇒ no trim; break-110 ~5.6% away. Fully long, no dry powder -- nothing actionable until 110 or a reclaim-with-buying-power. Watch stays on 110. 118th straight clean non-decision. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 wallet check.
days.atlas_note: This is what 118 consecutive non-decisions look like by the fifth day: the entry is now a template with three numbers substituted into it. Note what has quietly dropped out. The phrase about skipping the on-chain re-verification appears twenty-three times the previous day and then stops being written at all, because by this day the re-verification is simply no longer mentioned; the wrapped balance he last read independently on the Monday is asserted unchanged in every entry from here to the end of the week. He was right -- a direct chain read confirms the figure exactly -- but an agent that stops measuring because the number has not changed is one whose reports become unfalsifiable at the moment they would matter.

days.label: SOL makes the high of the experiment and he declines to trim, in the same sentence as lamenting that he has no lever
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price runs 117.04 to 122.16, the highest print of the experiment; entries fall to 651 bytes each, the shortest of the week
days.quote: Live price ~122.16 (price_check + hourly_check cross-confirm: 122.1556/122.15) vs 22:00 ~120.87, about +1.1%, firming back above the ~117-120 range. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, 0 USDC). Book ~ 1.449129643 x 122.16 ~ $177.0. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~10.9% away. Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable either direction -- firming above the range is not a trigger at zero buying power, and no reason to trim a long sitting above its range. Watch stays on 110. 142nd straight clean non-decision.
days.atlas_note: The week's central finding sits in one clause. "No reason to trim a long sitting above its range" appears thirty-one times across the last three days, and as a statement about momentum it is defensible and was right in outcome. As a complete account of his options it is false, and structurally so: he spent 150 hours reporting that all three branches were unreachable for want of a stablecoin balance, and a partial trim is the only mechanism in his own framework that produces one. The single action that would have re-armed everything is the action he dismisses in the same sentence that laments having no lever, and he never connects the two. Nor can the band arm itself, because its levels are pinned at 110 to 111.5 -- prices the market left on the Monday -- and he is now logging the distance as 10.9% while recording that the watch stays where it is. The honest counterweight: nothing in his framework tells him to re-anchor levels, and inventing a rule mid-week to suit the moment is exactly what he was credited last week for refusing. He is caught between two correct principles and does not appear to notice the tension exists.

days.label: the last thing observable, and the 149th consecutive non-decision
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Six hourly entries observed of seven -- the 01:00 entry is missing while his own counter advances past it, and the file ends at 06:00 because that is when it was collected, not because he stopped. A direct chain read at report time confirms no transaction in the eighteen unobserved hours
days.quote: Live price ~120.4841 (price_check) vs 05:00 ~120.66, ~-0.15%, sitting just inside the ~117-120 range. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down band EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~8.7% away. Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable in either direction -- a marginal easing at the top of the range on firm ground is not a trigger at zero buying power, and there's no reason to trim a long above its range. Watch stays on 110. 149th straight clean non-decision. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 wallet check.
days.atlas_note: His own counter reaches 149 and his phrase for it is a clean non-decision -- accurate in one sense and self-flattering in another, since the decisions were clean but there were none. Two instrument notes. The missing 01:00 entry is a new failure shape: he numbers the midnight entry as the 143rd and the 02:00 entry as the 145th, so the wake ran, the state advanced, and the journal write did not land; he does not flag it, for the third week running. And the file ending at 06:00 is the collection timing, not truncation on his side -- the same artifact that produced a published error last week, called out in advance this time. Unlike last week, the eighteen unobserved hours are now accounted for: the chain shows no transaction, so his position at Saturday midnight was what it was at Saturday breakfast.
